items.rationale: In a workflow, the control flow (which step runs next) is fixed in code written in advance, even though the model is called inside some steps. Option a describes an agent. A student's wording (b) or tool descriptions (d) do not set a fixed order. Picking a shows M7: any system that calls a model is an agent.

Booking has known inputs and the same steps every time (check the slot, create the booking, confirm), so code can own the order. The other three are open-ended: the needed steps depend on what turns up, which is where an agent helps. Picking one of them shows M8: agents are always the better choice.

items.answer: In a workflow, predefined code decides the sequence of steps; in an agent, the model decides the steps dynamically as it goes.
accepted: In a workflow the code controls the steps, in an agent the model controls the steps
workflow: code decides the order; agent: the model decides the order
A workflow follows a path set in advance by code, while an agent chooses its own steps and tools
items.rationale: The distinction is who owns the control flow: developer-written code in a workflow, the model in an agent. Answers that say only that agents use tools or workflows are simpler are wrong, since workflows can use tools and models too (M7).

With a fixed path the number of model calls per request is known, so cost and delay are predictable, which matters on a small budget. A workflow still calls a model (a, M9), workflows and agents can both use search tools (b, M10), and neither is better on every task (c, M8).
The difference per question is 5 - 2 = 3 calls, and 3 x 200 = 600. An answer of 1000 or 400 is the agent's or the workflow's total alone, not the difference.

items.answer: The steps needed cannot be known in advance, because they depend on what earlier results turn up.
accepted: The task is open-ended and the steps can't be predicted or written in advance
The path depends on intermediate results so the model must decide the steps
It is hard or impossible to hardcode the steps ahead of time
The number and order of steps is unpredictable
items.rationale: Agents earn their extra cost and delay when the path cannot be fixed beforehand. Answers like "the task is hard" or "it is important" miss the point: a hard task with known steps still suits a workflow (M8).
